name: Online community review and matching network
demand: There is evidence of existing discovery use, but no verified total seeker population, keyword volume, or app installs. Hive Index reports 5,855 communities across 294 topics and 36 platforms, with its homepage last updated 2026-10-21: https://thehiveindex.com/. Its traffic page lists monthly visitors of 4,268 for Dating and 1,243 for Entrepreneurship; Entrepreneurship showed 0/4 active promotions. These are competitor-published figures, with the measurement window and independent verification unspecified: https://thehiveindex.com/partners/traffic/. Hive Index’s Business report shows 19 reviews across 8 rated communities, suggesting review activity may be thin in at least that category: https://thehiveindex.com/topics/business/stats/. Unita claims 30,000 community seekers and owners visit monthly, but this is self-reported and unaudited: https://unita.co/sponsorship/.
prices: Hive Index lists free basic listings, Featured placement at $99 for 30 days, Gold at $390/year, and site sponsorship at $1,000/month. Its FAQ contradicts itself by describing Featured as both $99 one-time and $99/month, so confirm price before benchmarking: https://thehiveindex.com/submit/. Unita advertises sponsorship at $1,000/month or $1,500/month for its full package; its audience figures are self-reported: https://unita.co/sponsorship/. Discordium lists Discord-specific premium plans at €4.99, €12.99, and €29.99/month, with several analytics features marked as coming soon: https://discordium.de/premium.

revenue_proof.claim: Hive Index’s homepage displays “Sponsored this month by Altium.” This is a current sponsorship claim, but the fee, whether it was paid or in-kind, and an invoice or transaction are not public; treat verified revenue as unproven.
revenue_proof.claim_event_date: 2026-10 (homepage says “this month”; underlying transaction date unverified)

copy_speed: The direct incumbents already include Hive Index and Unita, so the core directory-and-review concept is not novel: https://thehiveindex.com/ and https://unita.co/. Since April 2026, Community Stack says its Engine Community Edition and Junction launched 2026-10-16; Junction includes a directory and cross-community discovery for technical communities: https://www.communitystack.io/about. UpStart launched 2026-07-05 and indexes startup directories and communities, an adjacent rather than exact competitor: https://open-launch.com/projects/upstart. OpenCommunity describes a 700+ community directory in an article dated 2026-08-01 and updated 2026-10-18; its product launch date is unverified: https://www.opencommunity.directory/blog/9-best-online-communities-for-entrepreneurs-in-2026. I found no exact like-for-like new launch with a verified date in this search.
platform_risk: High if the data strategy depends on scraping or platform APIs. Hive Index requires prior written permission for scraping, bulk reuse, or creating a competing directory substantially derived from its listings: https://thehiveindex.com/data-license/. Reddit’s current Data API terms say commercial use may require a separate agreement and restrict retention and use: https://redditinc.com/policies/data-api-terms. Discord prohibits scraping and commercializing API data: https://support-dev.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/8563934450327-Discord-Developer-Policy. SEO is viable only with useful original pages; Google identifies mass-produced, low-value pages, including AI-generated or scraped pages, as scaled-content abuse: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies.
defensible_asset: Potential compiled-data and review-network moat, but none exists at launch. First-party owner submissions, dated freshness checks, genuine member reviews, and cross-platform comparison could compound into a useful dataset. That advantage is not established by the concept itself: Hive Index already reports 5,855 listings, while its Business report has 19 reviews across 8 rated communities, and Unita also offers community reviews. Build an independently sourced dataset; Hive Index’s license bars a competing directory substantially derived from its data: https://thehiveindex.com/about/, https://thehiveindex.com/topics/business/stats/, https://unita.co/, https://thehiveindex.com/data-license/.
build_effort: Assessment: moderate for a narrow web MVP; high for a broad, trustworthy cross-platform index. Search, filters, owner submissions, reviews, and self-serve paid placement are conventional product features, but data rights, freshness, review abuse, and initial coverage are the hard parts. No verified build-hours estimate found. Avoid relying on scraped Hive, Reddit, or Discord data; their published terms constrain that route: https://thehiveindex.com/data-license/, https://redditinc.com/policies/data-api-terms, https://support-dev.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/8563934450327-Discord-Developer-Policy.
channel: Use useful original SEO pages, permissioned marketplace or community submissions, app-store listings if a native app is later justified, contextual paid ads, and opt-in partnerships. Do not send cold email, SMS, DMs, or calls. UK ICO guidance treats email, text, social DMs, and calls as direct marketing and says consent is often required for individual subscribers: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guide-to-pecr/electronic-and-telephone-marketing/. Reviews need careful handling: UK CMA guidance covers businesses publishing online reviews, and the US FTC rule prohibits fake reviews and incentives conditioned on positive or negative sentiment: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/fake-reviews, https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2024/08/federal-trade-commission-announces-final-rule-banning-fake-reviews-and-testimonials. Requirements in other target countries remain to be checked.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified. ≤5 hours/week is a post-launch design target only if listings are self-submitted, billing is self-serve, and agents handle routine freshness checks and triage. Initial seeding, review disputes, and channel setup may exceed it.
automation_reason: Estimate, not measured: agents could handle submission intake, deduplication, link checks, topic tagging, routine support drafts, moderation triage, and listing analytics. Human work remains for disputed reviews, rights and privacy decisions, fraud appeals, partner decisions, and acquisition strategy. The estimate assumes self-service submissions and checkout; Hive Index itself uses free owner submissions and paid self-serve listing options: https://thehiveindex.com/submit/.
moat_assessment: Conditional pass only if the product earns a permissioned, maintained dataset and a genuine review-contribution loop. The proposed moat is plausible but currently unproven; basic directory pages and topic tags are readily copied. There are no demonstrated switching costs, and network effects would require active users and community operators to contribute better data than existing directories. Hive Index’s scale and data license make independent acquisition of listings essential: https://thehiveindex.com/about/, https://thehiveindex.com/data-license/.
desk_test: Within one day, pick one niche and publish a simple page with a small set of owner-submitted listings, a review prompt, and a clearly disclosed Featured offer priced at Hive Index’s stated one-time $99 for 30 days. Share it only in channels that permit promotion or through opt-in partners; optionally use contextual search ads. Track real seeker signups, owner submissions, and an actual paid reservation. No cold messages and no copying Hive Index’s dataset. Stop if neither seekers nor operators take the relevant action: https://thehiveindex.com/submit/, https://thehiveindex.com/data-license/.
red_flags: The main incumbent is already broad, free to browse, and has reviews, owner analytics, and paid placements: https://thehiveindex.com/about/. Hive’s own traffic page shows many topic pages with 0/4 active promotions, so the paying-operator market is not proven by its price list: https://thehiveindex.com/partners/traffic/. Featured pricing is internally inconsistent, and no verified revenue, churn, profit, or paid-customer count was found. Review density appears limited in the Business category; fake or manipulated reviews create compliance and trust risk: https://thehiveindex.com/submit/, https://thehiveindex.com/topics/business/stats/, https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/fake-reviews.
